nodes.title: Device registers a media session
nodes.say: Every call begins with a client registering a media session that names its surface type; the Android companion's device bridge carries phone automation, not voice.

nodes.title: Where calls start
nodes.say: A call can come from the desktop tray or mascot, a web browser or desk terminal, or a meeting bot, and each is trusted as a different surface. Choose the device.
nodes.decidedBy: surface_type in the POST /media/sessions body; admitted_surface_type keeps a claimed surface only for a verified app session (else Unknown), then voice_surface_derivation maps it to a source surface

options.label: Desktop tray or mascot
options.say: The macOS, Windows or Linux tray or mascot app holds push-to-talk and becomes the owner's global live surface.

options.label: Web browser or ESP desk terminal
options.say: The web app on desktop or mobile, or the ESP32 desk terminal, becomes the ordinary realtime voice surface.

options.label: Meeting bot or unrecognised client
options.say: The meeting bot, or any client that cannot prove what it is, is treated as a shared room, never as the owner.

nodes.title: Tray becomes global live PTT
nodes.say: A tray registration resolves to the global live push-to-talk surface; its separate bridge socket carries screen frames and ambient audio, while the call rides voice control.

nodes.title: Web becomes realtime voice
nodes.say: A browser or desk terminal resolves to the realtime voice surface, which unlocks expanded guided grammar and is the only surface allowed concurrent voice requests.

nodes.title: Fail closed to a room
nodes.say: A meeting bot or unidentified client gets the meeting-room surface, so the call is answered by the room's envoy agent and never inherits owner authority.

nodes.title: Control socket accepted
nodes.say: The control route checks origin, principal and workspace ownership, loads the wake-name preference, builds a voice orchestrator, then starts one actor that owns this call.

nodes.title: Session start requested
nodes.say: The start frame names the chat on screen, voice mode and optional realtime profile. The call binds to that owned conversation instead of guessing between chat tabs.

nodes.title: Voice engines
nodes.say: Six speech engines can listen and talk on a call. Pick the one to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: session.start voice_mode=hands_free picks Magician's cascade; otherwise session.start realtime_profile, else llm.router.realtime_voice.operation_mapping.voice_controller (default voice_realtime_default) in magician-config.yaml; that profile's provider string picks the builder

options.label: OpenAI Realtime, server-proxied
options.say: Provider openai_realtime_backend, the profile the desktop tray asks for: Magician holds the socket to OpenAI and relays audio.

options.label: OpenAI Realtime, browser WebRTC
options.say: Provider openai_realtime, the default mapping: the browser talks to OpenAI directly with a short-lived token.

options.label: Gemini Live
options.say: Provider gemini_live: Google's live audio model, proxied through Magician over a WebSocket.

options.label: Grok voice
options.say: Provider grok_voice: xAI speech-to-speech, spoken through the same reader as OpenAI's backend socket.

options.label: GPT Live 1
options.say: Provider openai_live: a full-duplex speaking front end that hands all thinking back to Magician.

options.label: Magician hands-free cascade
options.say: Voice mode hands_free: local voice detection, streaming speech to text, a chat turn, then text to speech.

nodes.title: Server-proxied OpenAI session
nodes.say: For the backend profile, the OpenAI provider returns a backend-proxied descriptor, so Magician keeps the real key and relays every audio frame itself.

nodes.title: Browser token minted
nodes.say: For the browser profile, Magician mints an ephemeral OpenAI client secret and hands back a WebRTC address, so audio flows browser to OpenAI without crossing Magician.

nodes.title: Gemini Live socket
nodes.say: Gemini Live keeps the key server-side, forwards 24 kilohertz PCM to Google, and validates thinking and tool scheduling options against the model family.
nodes.evidence: magicllm/src/realtime/factory.rs:108; magicllm/src/realtime/gemini.rs:1; magicllm/src/realtime/gemini.rs:195; branch at magicllm/src/realtime/gemini.rs:367; branch at magicllm/src/realtime/gemini.rs:373

nodes.title: Grok voice socket
nodes.say: Grok voice reuses the OpenAI realtime provider in backend-proxied mode, only swapping in xAI's flatter session update payload and its own API key.

nodes.title: GPT Live mouth
nodes.say: GPT Live uses its own speaking prompt and no tool list. Magician records its policy snapshot without waiting for chat memory, then handles delegated work.

nodes.title: Hands-free cascade composed
nodes.say: The hands-free provider resolves the hands-free audio profile into a pipeline: Silero voice detection, Parakeet streaming speech recognition, then a text to speech chain.

nodes.title: Grounding gate
nodes.say: Only OpenAI realtime can hold a reply until memory is retrieved; other profiles must opt out explicitly, or Magician swaps in a grounded fallback profile.

nodes.title: Session minted
nodes.say: The orchestrator mints the upstream session, applies the preferred voice and turn detection, and for backend-proxied engines opens the audio channel straight away.

nodes.title: Where speech becomes text
nodes.say: The caller's speech becomes trusted text on this Mac, at the provider, or in the browser's own session. Choose one.
nodes.decidedBy: descriptor_requests_local_transcript: backend-proxied OpenAI with transcription_model: local (set on voice_realtime_openai_backend, fallback whisper-1); the hands-free cascade always uses media.surface_profiles hands_free streaming_stt; browser WebRTC calls report transcripts from the client

options.label: On this Mac
options.say: The same microphone audio is teed into the local FluidAudio, macOS Speech, then cloud fallback chain.

options.label: At the provider
options.say: The realtime provider transcribes its own input, as with Gemini, Grok, or OpenAI when local is not set or fails.

options.label: In the browser's WebRTC session
options.say: Audio never reaches Magician; the browser sends finished transcripts back over the control socket.

nodes.title: Local transcript attached
nodes.say: Before announcing ready, Magician opens a call-scoped local transcription stream; if it cannot start, the profile's vendor transcription model is restored.

nodes.title: Native engine wakes
nodes.say: On first use the FluidAudio manager spawns the native macOS audio engine with a fresh token, so Parakeet speech recognition runs on the device.

nodes.title: Provider transcribes
nodes.say: The provider's own input transcription produces the user's words, arriving as completed transcription events that Magician turns into finalized user transcripts.
nodes.evidence: magicllm/src/realtime/openai.rs:1166; magicllm/src/realtime/gemini.rs:1334; magician-api/src/voice_control_handler.rs:5157; branch at magicllm/src/realtime/openai.rs:1111; branch at magicllm/src/realtime/openai.rs:1140; branch at magicllm/src/realtime/openai.rs:1138

nodes.title: Browser reports transcripts
nodes.say: Direct WebRTC clients send user and assistant transcript frames themselves; on backend-proxied calls those caller-authored frames are ignored so they cannot be forged.

nodes.title: Audio frames routed
nodes.say: Each binary microphone frame is dropped while the assistant talks in half-duplex mode; otherwise it is copied to local transcription and sent to the provider.

nodes.title: Provider link opened
nodes.say: A background task connects to the provider's realtime WebSocket, sends a bootstrap session update, then forwards every microphone frame as a base64 audio append.

nodes.title: Provider events translated
nodes.say: Provider events become neutral signals: speech started and stopped, finalized transcripts, function calls, and audio chunks decoded into playable sound.

nodes.title: Utterance admitted
nodes.say: A final user transcript must pass the self-echo check and the wake-name gate before it is echoed to the client and allowed to start a turn.

nodes.title: Self-echo and wake name
nodes.say: Text that matches the assistant's own recent speech is rejected as echo, then the address gate requires the agent's name unless a follow-up window is open.

nodes.title: Who answers
nodes.say: The realtime model can answer directly, or Magician can run a full chat turn and speak the result. Pick which to follow.

options.label: The realtime model
options.say: The realtime model replies in its own voice once the turn is grounded.

options.label: Hands-free chat turn
options.say: The utterance becomes a complete chat turn, and its answer is synthesized locally.

nodes.title: Memory context retrieved
nodes.say: The turn is opened in the chat ledger and, for OpenAI, the reply is held until memory and procedure context for this utterance has been retrieved.

nodes.title: Tools during a call
nodes.say: The voice model can just talk, call a direct voice tool, or hand real work to chat. Choose which to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: the provider emits a FunctionCall event (OpenAI response.function_call_arguments.done) or a direct client sends tool.dispatch; the tool name delegate_to_chat takes the chat detour

options.label: No, it just answers
options.say: The model speaks its reply directly with no tool involved.

options.label: A direct voice tool
options.say: One catalog tool runs under chat policy and its short result goes back to the model.

options.label: Delegate to chat
options.say: Real work is handed to the full chat agent in the background while the voice keeps talking.

nodes.title: Direct tool dispatched
nodes.say: The orchestrator checks the call against the advertised policy snapshot, runs it through chat's external tool dispatcher, and returns a speakable summary to the model.

nodes.title: Handed off to chat
nodes.say: Delegate to chat acks at once and runs a background chat engine turn, the same path a typed chat message takes, while the voice call continues.
nodes.evidence: magician-media/src/media_rails/voice_orchestrator.rs:2987; magician-media/src/media_rails/voice_orchestrator.rs:3029; magician-media/src/media_rails/voice_orchestrator.rs:3828; branch at magician-media/src/media_rails/voice_orchestrator.rs:2822; branch at magician-media/src/media_rails/voice_orchestrator.rs:2742; branch at magician-media/src/media_rails/voice_orchestrator.rs:2808

nodes.title: Chat chunks spoken
nodes.say: As the chat turn streams, each speakable chunk is injected into the live provider session as a system message, so the voice reads progress aloud.

nodes.title: Full chat turn runs
nodes.say: In hands-free mode the utterance runs as a complete chat turn with tools and delegation, on the execution runtime rather than the voice worker.

nodes.title: Answer synthesized
nodes.say: The reply is spoken by the first working text to speech provider in the chain, starting with Kokoro on FluidAudio and then macOS speech.

nodes.title: Speech plays back
nodes.say: Each spoken reply chunk is measured for echo suppression, then written back as a binary frame that the device plays through its speaker.

nodes.title: Interruptions
nodes.say: The caller can let the reply play out, or talk over it to cut it short. Pick one.
nodes.decidedBy: a ptt.engage frame while a provider or cascaded response is still playing

options.label: No, it plays out
options.say: The reply finishes and both sides of the turn are recorded.

options.label: User barges in
options.say: Pressing talk again cancels the reply that is still playing.

nodes.title: Barge-in cancels
nodes.say: Push-to-talk during a reply sends an interrupt control, which the provider task turns into an OpenAI response cancel, or stops the cascaded speech.

nodes.title: Transcript lands in chat
nodes.say: User and assistant transcripts go out as chat message events tagged with the voice channel, so they are saved and appear live in the chat thread.

nodes.title: Call hangs up
nodes.say: When the caller ends the session, the local transcript stream closes and the provider is asked to close and report its final usage before cleanup.

nodes.title: Call ended
nodes.say: One socket, one orchestrator, swappable speech engines, and every spoken word ends up in the chat thread.
